Sentence (English): I checked the dishwasher after washing.
Comments (English): [ That's good ] || ---------------- || Wow, the box is much larger than I expected. I thought it was about the size of an oven-type air fryer, but it's a bit bigger. The packaging is well-made with Styrofoam. The components inside are very well-packaged. No separate installation is required, so you can use it anywhere with space for a power cord and drainage. The power cord is short, so you'll need a nearby outlet. There are five modes: Standard, Strong, Eco, and Rapid Steam, so you can choose the one you want. There's also a timer function. The Rapid mode allows for a quick 30-minute wash. The dishwasher uses 72-degree high-pressure water, 360-degree rotations in two stages, and it's sprayed without any blind spots, thoroughly removing grease, chili powder, rice paste, and other debris, leaving dishes as clean as if they were washed by hand. It also has a 72-hour air circulation function for dish storage. However, this feature might be a bit of a concern for your electricity bill. It also uses only 5 liters of water, significantly saving water compared to washing dishes by hand, reducing water waste. The dish rack is also equipped with wheels for smooth loading and removal. There's an LED lamp at the top of the dishwasher, which lights up when you open the door after washing, allowing you to remove dishes even in the dark. It's said that arranging dishes so they face each other from left to right during washing is more effective. It's also said that briefly rinsing dishes before placing them in the dishwasher will help ensure a cleaner wash. I'm so happy that the tedious task of washing dishes will be so much easier. There are some things you must keep in mind before using the dishwasher. The water inlet is located at the top of the machine, and you can fill it with water using the water inlet. Make sure the machine is turned on. A faucet icon will appear on the time display. Check this before filling. The water level sensor will sound an alarm when the water level reaches the level. The faucet icon will disappear. Then, you can stop the water supply and continue using the machine. Checkpoints: The most important thing is to always turn the machine on while filling! And use a dishwasher-specific detergent! Remember these two things. You must hold down the power button for 2-3 seconds to turn it on. Forced water drains by pressing the steam sterilization button and the preset button simultaneously for 3 seconds. However, this function is said to be used when moving the product when not in use for a long period of time, so use with caution. I haven't tried washing dishes yet, but I've only tried it, and the water flow is quite strong. It's quite noisy, and the sink floor vibrates, so using a noise-absorbing mat might be a good idea. I'll add a review after washing the dishes. While the instructions and operation aren't difficult, I recommend reading the manual carefully before use even if you know how to use it. I'll add a review after use. First, the vibration and noise were reduced after I put the dishes in and spun them. I stir-fried dakgalbi (spicy stir-fried chicken) and then rinsed it with water. I stacked the dishes with the bottom facing down because it was difficult to arrange them as instructed. I thought the regular mode would take longer, so I used the quick mode. The oil, red pepper powder, and kimchi were all cleaned cleanly. However, there was a dakgalbi smell. Could the smell be due to the detergent? I checked the dishwasher after washing. There was some chicken galbi grease on both corners of the front door. There was a rubber gasket underneath the door, and a lot of grease was also stained there. I removed the rubber gasket and wiped it with a wet tissue. I think cleaning this part is important. It also has a 72-hour air circulation function for dish storage. However, this feature might be a bit of a concern for your electricity bill. It also uses only 5 liters of water, significantly saving water compared to washing dishes by hand, reducing water waste. The dish rack is also equipped with wheels for smooth loading and removal. There's an LED lamp at the top of the dishwasher, which lights up when you open the door after washing, allowing you to remove dishes even in the dark. It's said that arranging dishes so they face each other from left to right during washing is more effective. It's also said that briefly rinsing dishes before placing them in the dishwasher will help ensure a cleaner wash. I'm so happy that the tedious task of washing dishes will be so much easier. There are some things you must keep in mind before using the dishwasher. The water inlet is located at the top of the machine, and you can fill it with water using the water inlet. Make sure the machine is turned on. A faucet icon will appear on the time display. Check this before filling. The water level sensor will sound an alarm when the water level reaches the level. The faucet icon will disappear. Then, you can stop the water supply and continue using the machine. Checkpoints: The most important thing is to always turn the machine on while filling! And use a dishwasher-specific detergent! Remember these two things. You must hold down the power button for 2-3 seconds to turn it on. Forced water drains by pressing the steam sterilization button and the preset button simultaneously for 3 seconds. However, this function is said to be used when moving the product when not in use for a long period of time, so use with caution. I haven't tried washing dishes yet, but I've only tried it, and the water flow is quite strong. It's quite noisy, and the sink floor vibrates, so using a noise-absorbing mat might be a good idea. I'll add a review after washing the dishes. While the instructions and operation aren't difficult, I recommend reading the manual carefully before use even if you know how to use it. I'll add a review after use. First, the vibration and noise were reduced after I put the dishes in and spun them. I stir-fried dakgalbi (spicy stir-fried chicken) and then rinsed it with water. I stacked the dishes with the bottom facing down because it was difficult to arrange them as instructed. I thought the regular mode would take longer, so I used the quick mode. The oil, red pepper powder, and kimchi were all cleaned cleanly. However, there was a dakgalbi smell. Could the smell be due to the detergent? I checked the dishwasher after washing. There was some chicken galbi grease on both corners of the front door. There was a rubber gasket underneath the door, and a lot of grease was also stained there. I removed the rubber gasket and wiped it with a wet tissue. I think cleaning this part is important. It's said that arranging dishes so they face each other from left to right during washing is more effective. It's also said that briefly rinsing dishes before placing them in the dishwasher will help ensure a cleaner wash. I'm so happy that the tedious task of washing dishes will be so much easier. There are some things you must keep in mind before using the dishwasher. The water inlet is located at the top of the machine, and you can fill it with water using the water inlet. The faucet icon will disappear. Then, you can stop the water supply and continue using the machine. Checkpoints: The most important thing is to always turn the machine on while filling! And use a dishwasher-specific detergent! Remember these two things. You must hold down the power button for 2-3 seconds to turn it on. Forced water drains by pressing the steam sterilization button and the preset button simultaneously for 3 seconds. However, this function is said to be used when moving the product when not in use for a long period of time, so use with caution. I'll add a review after washing the dishes. While the instructions and operation aren't difficult, I recommend reading the manual carefully before use even if you know how to use it. I'll add a review after use. First, the vibration and noise were reduced after I put the dishes in and spun them. I stir-fried dakgalbi (spicy stir-fried chicken) and then rinsed it with water. I stacked the dishes with the bottom facing down because it was difficult to arrange them as instructed. I thought the regular mode would take longer, so I used the quick mode. The oil, red pepper powder, and kimchi were all cleaned cleanly. However, there was a dakgalbi smell. Could the smell be due to the detergent? I checked the dishwasher after washing. There was some chicken galbi grease on both corners of the front door. There was a rubber gasket underneath the door, and a lot of grease was also stained there. I removed the rubber gasket and wiped it with a wet tissue. I think cleaning this part is important. Comments (English): [ That's good ] || ---------------- || Wow, the box is much larger than I expected. I thought it was about the size of an oven-type air fryer, but it's a bit bigger. The packaging is well-made with Styrofoam. The components inside are very well-packaged. No separate installation is required, so you can use it anywhere with space for a power cord and drainage. The power cord is short, so you'll need a nearby outlet. There are five modes: Standard, Strong, Eco, and Rapid Steam, so you can choose the one you want. There's also a timer function. The Rapid mode allows for a quick 30-minute wash. The dishwasher uses 72-degree high-pressure water, 360-degree rotations in two stages, and it's sprayed without any blind spots, thoroughly removing grease, chili powder, rice paste, and other debris, leaving dishes as clean as if they were washed by hand. It also has a 72-hour air circulation function for dish storage. However, this feature might be a bit of a concern for your electricity bill. It also uses only 5 liters of water, significantly saving water compared to washing dishes by hand, reducing water waste. The dish rack is also equipped with wheels for smooth loading and removal. There's an LED lamp at the top of the dishwasher, which lights up when you open the door after washing, allowing you to remove dishes even in the dark. It's said that arranging dishes so they face each other from left to right during washing is more effective. It's also said that briefly rinsing dishes before placing them in the dishwasher will help ensure a cleaner wash. I'm so happy that the tedious task of washing dishes will be so much easier. There are some things you must keep in mind before using the dishwasher. The water inlet is located at the top of the machine, and you can fill it with water using the water inlet. Make sure the machine is turned on. A faucet icon will appear on the time display. Check this before filling. The water level sensor will sound an alarm when the water level reaches the level. The faucet icon will disappear. Then, you can stop the water supply and continue using the machine. Checkpoints: The most important thing is to always turn the machine on while filling! And use a dishwasher-specific detergent! Remember these two things. You must hold down the power button for 2-3 seconds to turn it on. Forced water drains by pressing the steam sterilization button and the preset button simultaneously for 3 seconds. However, this function is said to be used when moving the product when not in use for a long period of time, so use with caution. I haven't tried washing dishes yet, but I've only tried it, and the water flow is quite strong. It's quite noisy, and the sink floor vibrates, so using a noise-absorbing mat might be a good idea. I'll add a review after washing the dishes. While the instructions and operation aren't difficult, I recommend reading the manual carefully before use even if you know how to use it. I'll add a review after use. First, the vibration and noise were reduced after I put the dishes in and spun them. I stir-fried dakgalbi (spicy stir-fried chicken) and then rinsed it with water. I stacked the dishes with the bottom facing down because it was difficult to arrange them as instructed. I thought the regular mode would take longer, so I used the quick mode. The oil, red pepper powder, and kimchi were all cleaned cleanly. However, there was a dakgalbi smell. Could the smell be due to the detergent? I checked the dishwasher after washing. There was some chicken galbi grease on both corners of the front door. There was a rubber gasket underneath the door, and a lot of grease was also stained there. I removed the rubber gasket and wiped it with a wet tissue. I think cleaning this part is important. Comments (English): [ I ignored it because it was small, but it unexpectedly became an essential item. ] || ---------------- || We're a three-person household that doesn't cook much at home. I've always wanted a dishwasher, but our kitchen is too small, and we don't cook a lot, so my husband's opposition prevented us from bringing in a dishwasher. Sadly, we can't drill holes in our kitchen. We can't drill holes for the water inlet and outlet, or do whatever we want with the kitchen cabinets. Installing a large dishwasher was almost out of the question. Then, I discovered this minimalist dishwasher and decided to get it. My criteria for a dishwasher were: 1. Minimal size, not taking up too much space in the kitchen, and easy to drill holes and install. - Installation is incredibly simple! Just find a level spot, attach the drain hose, and place it where it drains. It's easier to just fill the water tank yourself. I think I fill the large water tank four or five times. When the water level is just right, you'll hear a beep, and then you should immediately stop the water supply. 2. It's easy to use. - Just fill it with water, add detergent, and press the desired mode. It couldn't be simpler. 3. Even the mini-size dishwasher is large enough to fit my largest plates. - We're a family of three, and we don't eat a lot or cook very often. So, when cups or small dishes come out, I just pre-wash them and put them away before I return them. The largest plate is a flat white IKEA plate, and it fits if you tilt it sideways. I think people who often use large plates might find it a bit difficult to use. It's a good size for things like rice bowls, soup bowls, cups, spoons, and side plates. This dishwasher fits my lifestyle. If it were too large, it wouldn't get through this quickly, and if I had to load a lot at once, it would be burdensome and the dishes would pile up. ***. As I continued to use it, I realized there were more minor drawbacks than I expected. 1. The water filling process requires a lot of concentration! - Many reviews mention error messages, but I never thought I'd be the one experiencing that error. I got an E4 error! This is really important. They say you have to plug in the dishwasher, turn on the power button, and then add water to avoid this error. I knew this from previous product reviews, so I thought I could use it with confidence. But then my husband, after installing it, thoughtlessly poured water into it without turning on the power button. And when he did, an E4 error message appeared. I found blog reviews that suggested draining all the water, thoroughly cleaning it, and then trying again. So I drained all the water, dried it, and bled it completely dry. After repeated error messages and drying, I finally got it to work. I urge you all to read my review and keep this in mind! Always turn on the power before adding water. And when you hear a beeping sound while adding water, immediately stop the water supply. This is a real water stress. 2. Drying and ventilation functions. These are there, but they're not very effective. This is the most disappointing feature. After the dishwasher finishes washing, it seems to gently circulate the air to dry the dishes. It's supposed to continue blowing air and drying the dishes if you don't open the door. However, the ventilation function is so weak that I've never seen dishes that were completely dry by the next day. So, leaving the door open actually dries them better. The problem is, the door gets in the way when you open it. So, I bought a safety device from Daiso that keeps the door slightly open. The door can either be completely closed or completely open, two extremes. While there are some drawbacks, I'm satisfied with the price. I always consider price when purchasing appliances, so I don't want to be a greedy person. If drying is important to you, you should look for a product with additional functions. My husband, who said he wouldn't use it because it was a hassle to fill the water, is more diligent than anyone else at filling the water and running the dishwasher. I've always wanted a dishwasher, but our kitchen is too small, and we don't cook a lot, so my husband's opposition prevented us from bringing in a dishwasher. Sadly, we can't drill holes in our kitchen. We can't drill holes for the water inlet and outlet, or do whatever we want with the kitchen cabinets. Installing a large dishwasher was almost out of the question. Then, I discovered this minimalist dishwasher and decided to get it. My criteria for a dishwasher were: 1. Minimal size, not taking up too much space in the kitchen, and easy to drill holes and install. - Installation is incredibly simple! Just find a level spot, attach the drain hose, and place it where it drains. It's easier to just fill the water tank yourself. I think I fill the large water tank four or five times. When the water level is just right, you'll hear a beep, and then you should immediately stop the water supply. 2. It's easy to use. - Just fill it with water, add detergent, and press the desired mode. It couldn't be simpler. 3. Even the mini-size dishwasher is large enough to fit my largest plates. - We're a family of three, and we don't eat a lot or cook very often. So, when cups or small dishes come out, I just pre-wash them and put them away before I return them. The largest plate is a flat white IKEA plate, and it fits if you tilt it sideways. I think people who often use large plates might find it a bit difficult to use. It's a good size for things like rice bowls, soup bowls, cups, spoons, and side plates. This dishwasher fits my lifestyle. If it were too large, it wouldn't get through this quickly, and if I had to load a lot at once, it would be burdensome and the dishes would pile up. ***. As I continued to use it, I realized there were more minor drawbacks than I expected. 1. The water filling process requires a lot of concentration! - Many reviews mention error messages, but I never thought I'd be the one experiencing that error. I got an E4 error! This is really important. They say you have to plug in the dishwasher, turn on the power button, and then add water to avoid this error. I knew this from previous product reviews, so I thought I could use it with confidence. But then my husband, after installing it, thoughtlessly poured water into it without turning on the power button. And when he did, an E4 error message appeared. I found blog reviews that suggested draining all the water, thoroughly cleaning it, and then trying again. So I drained all the water, dried it, and bled it completely dry. After repeated error messages and drying, I finally got it to work. I urge you all to read my review and keep this in mind! Always turn on the power before adding water. And when you hear a beeping sound while adding water, immediately stop the water supply. This is a real water stress. 2. Drying and ventilation functions. These are there, but they're not very effective. This is the most disappointing feature. After the dishwasher finishes washing, it seems to gently circulate the air to dry the dishes. It's supposed to continue blowing air and drying the dishes if you don't open the door. However, the ventilation function is so weak that I've never seen dishes that were completely dry by the next day. So, leaving the door open actually dries them better. The problem is, the door gets in the way when you open it. So, I bought a safety device from Daiso that keeps the door slightly open. The door can either be completely closed or completely open, two extremes. While there are some drawbacks, I'm satisfied with the price. I always consider price when purchasing appliances, so I don't want to be a greedy person. If drying is important to you, you should look for a product with additional functions. My husband, who said he wouldn't use it because it was a hassle to fill the water, is more diligent than anyone else at filling the water and running the dishwasher. Sadly, we can't drill holes in our kitchen. We can't drill holes for the water inlet and outlet, or do whatever we want with the kitchen cabinets. Installing a large dishwasher was almost out of the question. Then, I discovered this minimalist dishwasher and decided to get it. My criteria for a dishwasher were: 1. Minimal size, not taking up too much space in the kitchen, and easy to drill holes and install. - Installation is incredibly simple! Just find a level spot, attach the drain hose, and place it where it drains. It's easier to just fill the water tank yourself. I think I fill the large water tank four or five times. When the water level is just right, you'll hear a beep, and then you should immediately stop the water supply. 2. It's easy to use. - Just fill it with water, add detergent, and press the desired mode. It couldn't be simpler. 3. Even the mini-size dishwasher is large enough to fit my largest plates. - We're a family of three, and we don't eat a lot or cook very often. So, when cups or small dishes come out, I just pre-wash them and put them away before I return them. The largest plate is a flat white IKEA plate, and it fits if you tilt it sideways. I think people who often use large plates might find it a bit difficult to use. It's a good size for things like rice bowls, soup bowls, cups, spoons, and side plates. This dishwasher fits my lifestyle. If it were too large, it wouldn't get through this quickly, and if I had to load a lot at once, it would be burdensome and the dishes would pile up. ***. As I continued to use it, I realized there were more minor drawbacks than I expected. 1. The water filling process requires a lot of concentration! - Many reviews mention error messages, but I never thought I'd be the one experiencing that error. I got an E4 error! This is really important. They say you have to plug in the dishwasher, turn on the power button, and then add water to avoid this error. I knew this from previous product reviews, so I thought I could use it with confidence. But then my husband, after installing it, thoughtlessly poured water into it without turning on the power button. And when he did, an E4 error message appeared. I found blog reviews that suggested draining all the water, thoroughly cleaning it, and then trying again. So I drained all the water, dried it, and bled it completely dry. After repeated error messages and drying, I finally got it to work. I urge you all to read my review and keep this in mind! Always turn on the power before adding water. And when you hear a beeping sound while adding water, immediately stop the water supply. This is a real water stress. 2. Drying and ventilation functions. These are there, but they're not very effective. This is the most disappointing feature. After the dishwasher finishes washing, it seems to gently circulate the air to dry the dishes. It's supposed to continue blowing air and drying the dishes if you don't open the door. However, the ventilation function is so weak that I've never seen dishes that were completely dry by the next day. So, leaving the door open actually dries them better. The problem is, the door gets in the way when you open it. So, I bought a safety device from Daiso that keeps the door slightly open. The door can either be completely closed or completely open, two extremes. While there are some drawbacks, I'm satisfied with the price. I always consider price when purchasing appliances, so I don't want to be a greedy person. If drying is important to you, you should look for a product with additional functions. My husband, who said he wouldn't use it because it was a hassle to fill the water, is more diligent than anyone else at filling the water and running the dishwasher. This is a review written after receiving the product for free as part of the Coupang Experience Group event.

I've always wanted a dishwasher, but our kitchen is too small, and we don't cook a lot, so my husband's opposition prevented us from bringing in a dishwasher. Sadly, we can't drill holes in our kitchen. We can't drill holes for the water inlet and outlet, or do whatever we want with the kitchen cabinets. Installing a large dishwasher was almost out of the question. Then, I discovered this minimalist dishwasher and decided to get it. My criteria for a dishwasher were: 1. Minimal size, not taking up too much space in the kitchen, and easy to drill holes and install. - Installation is incredibly simple! Just find a level spot, attach the drain hose, and place it where it drains. It's easier to just fill the water tank yourself. I think I fill the large water tank four or five times. When the water level is just right, you'll hear a beep, and then you should immediately stop the water supply. 2. It's easy to use. - Just fill it with water, add detergent, and press the desired mode. It couldn't be simpler. 3. Even the mini-size dishwasher is large enough to fit my largest plates. - We're a family of three, and we don't eat a lot or cook very often. So, when cups or small dishes come out, I just pre-wash them and put them away before I return them. The largest plate is a flat white IKEA plate, and it fits if you tilt it sideways. I think people who often use large plates might find it a bit difficult to use. It's a good size for things like rice bowls, soup bowls, cups, spoons, and side plates. This dishwasher fits my lifestyle. If it were too large, it wouldn't get through this quickly, and if I had to load a lot at once, it would be burdensome and the dishes would pile up. ***. As I continued to use it, I realized there were more minor drawbacks than I expected. 1. The water filling process requires a lot of concentration! - Many reviews mention error messages, but I never thought I'd be the one experiencing that error. I got an E4 error! This is really important. They say you have to plug in the dishwasher, turn on the power button, and then add water to avoid this error. I knew this from previous product reviews, so I thought I could use it with confidence. But then my husband, after installing it, thoughtlessly poured water into it without turning on the power button. And when he did, an E4 error message appeared. I found blog reviews that suggested draining all the water, thoroughly cleaning it, and then trying again. So I drained all the water, dried it, and bled it completely dry. After repeated error messages and drying, I finally got it to work. I urge you all to read my review and keep this in mind! Always turn on the power before adding water. And when you hear a beeping sound while adding water, immediately stop the water supply. This is a real water stress. 2. Drying and ventilation functions. These are there, but they're not very effective. This is the most disappointing feature. After the dishwasher finishes washing, it seems to gently circulate the air to dry the dishes. It's supposed to continue blowing air and drying the dishes if you don't open the door. However, the ventilation function is so weak that I've never seen dishes that were completely dry by the next day. So, leaving the door open actually dries them better. The problem is, the door gets in the way when you open it. So, I bought a safety device from Daiso that keeps the door slightly open. The door can either be completely closed or completely open, two extremes. While there are some drawbacks, I'm satisfied with the price. I always consider price when purchasing appliances, so I don't want to be a greedy person. If drying is important to you, you should look for a product with additional functions. My husband, who said he wouldn't use it because it was a hassle to fill the water, is more diligent than anyone else at filling the water and running the dishwasher. This is a review written after receiving the product for free as part of the Coupang Experience Group event.

I've always wanted a dishwasher, but our kitchen is too small, and we don't cook a lot, so my husband's opposition prevented us from bringing in a dishwasher. Sadly, we can't drill holes in our kitchen. We can't drill holes for the water inlet and outlet, or do whatever we want with the kitchen cabinets. Installing a large dishwasher was almost out of the question. Then, I discovered this minimalist dishwasher and decided to get it. My criteria for a dishwasher were: 1. Minimal size, not taking up too much space in the kitchen, and easy to drill holes and install. - Installation is incredibly simple! Just find a level spot, attach the drain hose, and place it where it drains. It's easier to just fill the water tank yourself. I think I fill the large water tank four or five times. When the water level is just right, you'll hear a beep, and then you should immediately stop the water supply. 2. It's easy to use. - Just fill it with water, add detergent, and press the desired mode. It couldn't be simpler. 3. Even the mini-size dishwasher is large enough to fit my largest plates. - We're a family of three, and we don't eat a lot or cook very often. So, when cups or small dishes come out, I just pre-wash them and put them away before I return them. The largest plate is a flat white IKEA plate, and it fits if you tilt it sideways. I think people who often use large plates might find it a bit difficult to use. It's a good size for things like rice bowls, soup bowls, cups, spoons, and side plates. This dishwasher fits my lifestyle. If it were too large, it wouldn't get through this quickly, and if I had to load a lot at once, it would be burdensome and the dishes would pile up. ***. As I continued to use it, I realized there were more minor drawbacks than I expected. 1. The water filling process requires a lot of concentration! - Many reviews mention error messages, but I never thought I'd be the one experiencing that error. I got an E4 error! This is really important. They say you have to plug in the dishwasher, turn on the power button, and then add water to avoid this error. I knew this from previous product reviews, so I thought I could use it with confidence. But then my husband, after installing it, thoughtlessly poured water into it without turning on the power button. And when he did, an E4 error message appeared. I found blog reviews that suggested draining all the water, thoroughly cleaning it, and then trying again. So I drained all the water, dried it, and bled it completely dry. After repeated error messages and drying, I finally got it to work. I urge you all to read my review and keep this in mind! Always turn on the power before adding water. And when you hear a beeping sound while adding water, immediately stop the water supply. This is a real water stress. 2. Drying and ventilation functions. These are there, but they're not very effective. This is the most disappointing feature. After the dishwasher finishes washing, it seems to gently circulate the air to dry the dishes. It's supposed to continue blowing air and drying the dishes if you don't open the door. However, the ventilation function is so weak that I've never seen dishes that were completely dry by the next day. So, leaving the door open actually dries them better. The problem is, the door gets in the way when you open it. So, I bought a safety device from Daiso that keeps the door slightly open. The door can either be completely closed or completely open, two extremes. While there are some drawbacks, I'm satisfied with the price. I always consider price when purchasing appliances, so I don't want to be a greedy person. If drying is important to you, you should look for a product with additional functions. My husband, who said he wouldn't use it because it was a hassle to fill the water, is more diligent than anyone else at filling the water and running the dishwasher. This is a review written after receiving the product for free as part of the Coupang Experience Group event.

I think people who often use large plates might find it a bit difficult to use. It's a good size for things like rice bowls, soup bowls, cups, spoons, and side plates. I knew this from previous product reviews, so I thought I could use it with confidence. It's supposed to continue blowing air and drying the dishes if you don't open the door. However, the ventilation function is so weak that I've never seen dishes that were completely dry by the next day. So, leaving the door open actually dries them better. The problem is, the door gets in the way when you open it. So, I bought a safety device from Daiso that keeps the door slightly open. The door can either be completely closed or completely open, two extremes. While there are some drawbacks, I'm satisfied with the price. I always consider price when purchasing appliances, so I don't want to be a greedy person. If drying is important to you, you should look for a product with additional functions. My husband, who said he wouldn't use it because it was a hassle to fill the water, is more diligent than anyone else at filling the water and running the dishwasher. Sadly, we can't drill holes in our kitchen. We can't drill holes for the water inlet and outlet, or do whatever we want with the kitchen cabinets. Installing a large dishwasher was almost out of the question. Then, I discovered this minimalist dishwasher and decided to get it. My criteria for a dishwasher were: 1. Minimal size, not taking up too much space in the kitchen, and easy to drill holes and install. - Installation is incredibly simple! Just find a level spot, attach the drain hose, and place it where it drains. It's easier to just fill the water tank yourself. I think I fill the large water tank four or five times. When the water level is just right, you'll hear a beep, and then you should immediately stop the water supply. 2. It's easy to use. - Just fill it with water, add detergent, and press the desired mode. It couldn't be simpler. 3. Even the mini-size dishwasher is large enough to fit my largest plates. - We're a family of three, and we don't eat a lot or cook very often. So, when cups or small dishes come out, I just pre-wash them and put them away before I return them. The largest plate is a flat white IKEA plate, and it fits if you tilt it sideways. I think people who often use large plates might find it a bit difficult to use. It's a good size for things like rice bowls, soup bowls, cups, spoons, and side plates. This dishwasher fits my lifestyle. If it were too large, it wouldn't get through this quickly, and if I had to load a lot at once, it would be burdensome and the dishes would pile up. ***. As I continued to use it, I realized there were more minor drawbacks than I expected. 1. The water filling process requires a lot of concentration! - Many reviews mention error messages, but I never thought I'd be the one experiencing that error. I got an E4 error! This is really important. They say you have to plug in the dishwasher, turn on the power button, and then add water to avoid this error. I knew this from previous product reviews, so I thought I could use it with confidence. But then my husband, after installing it, thoughtlessly poured water into it without turning on the power button. And when he did, an E4 error message appeared. I found blog reviews that suggested draining all the water, thoroughly cleaning it, and then trying again. So I drained all the water, dried it, and bled it completely dry. After repeated error messages and drying, I finally got it to work. I urge you all to read my review and keep this in mind! Always turn on the power before adding water. And when you hear a beeping sound while adding water, immediately stop the water supply. This is a real water stress. 2. Drying and ventilation functions. These are there, but they're not very effective. This is the most disappointing feature. After the dishwasher finishes washing, it seems to gently circulate the air to dry the dishes. It's supposed to continue blowing air and drying the dishes if you don't open the door. However, the ventilation function is so weak that I've never seen dishes that were completely dry by the next day. So, leaving the door open actually dries them better. The problem is, the door gets in the way when you open it. So, I bought a safety device from Daiso that keeps the door slightly open. The door can either be completely closed or completely open, two extremes. While there are some drawbacks, I'm satisfied with the price. I always consider price when purchasing appliances, so I don't want to be a greedy person. If drying is important to you, you should look for a product with additional functions. My husband, who said he wouldn't use it because it was a hassle to fill the water, is more diligent than anyone else at filling the water and running the dishwasher. This is a review written after receiving the product for free as part of the Coupang Experience Group event.

Comments (English): [ I ignored it because it was small, but it unexpectedly became an essential item. ] || ---------------- || We're a three-person household that doesn't cook much at home. I've always wanted a dishwasher, but our kitchen is too small, and we don't cook a lot, so my husband's opposition prevented us from bringing in a dishwasher. Sadly, we can't drill holes in our kitchen. We can't drill holes for the water inlet and outlet, or do whatever we want with the kitchen cabinets. Installing a large dishwasher was almost out of the question. Then, I discovered this minimalist dishwasher and decided to get it. My criteria for a dishwasher were: 1. Minimal size, not taking up too much space in the kitchen, and easy to drill holes and install. - Installation is incredibly simple! Just find a level spot, attach the drain hose, and place it where it drains. It's easier to just fill the water tank yourself. I think I fill the large water tank four or five times. When the water level is just right, you'll hear a beep, and then you should immediately stop the water supply. 2. It's easy to use. - Just fill it with water, add detergent, and press the desired mode. It couldn't be simpler. 3. Even the mini-size dishwasher is large enough to fit my largest plates. - We're a family of three, and we don't eat a lot or cook very often. So, when cups or small dishes come out, I just pre-wash them and put them away before I return them. The largest plate is a flat white IKEA plate, and it fits if you tilt it sideways. I think people who often use large plates might find it a bit difficult to use. It's a good size for things like rice bowls, soup bowls, cups, spoons, and side plates. This dishwasher fits my lifestyle. If it were too large, it wouldn't get through this quickly, and if I had to load a lot at once, it would be burdensome and the dishes would pile up. ***. As I continued to use it, I realized there were more minor drawbacks than I expected. 1. The water filling process requires a lot of concentration! - Many reviews mention error messages, but I never thought I'd be the one experiencing that error. I got an E4 error! This is really important. They say you have to plug in the dishwasher, turn on the power button, and then add water to avoid this error. I knew this from previous product reviews, so I thought I could use it with confidence. But then my husband, after installing it, thoughtlessly poured water into it without turning on the power button. And when he did, an E4 error message appeared. I found blog reviews that suggested draining all the water, thoroughly cleaning it, and then trying again. So I drained all the water, dried it, and bled it completely dry. After repeated error messages and drying, I finally got it to work. I urge you all to read my review and keep this in mind! Always turn on the power before adding water. And when you hear a beeping sound while adding water, immediately stop the water supply. This is a real water stress. 2. Drying and ventilation functions. These are there, but they're not very effective. This is the most disappointing feature. After the dishwasher finishes washing, it seems to gently circulate the air to dry the dishes. It's supposed to continue blowing air and drying the dishes if you don't open the door. However, the ventilation function is so weak that I've never seen dishes that were completely dry by the next day. So, leaving the door open actually dries them better. The problem is, the door gets in the way when you open it. So, I bought a safety device from Daiso that keeps the door slightly open. The door can either be completely closed or completely open, two extremes. While there are some drawbacks, I'm satisfied with the price. I always consider price when purchasing appliances, so I don't want to be a greedy person. If drying is important to you, you should look for a product with additional functions. My husband, who said he wouldn't use it because it was a hassle to fill the water, is more diligent than anyone else at filling the water and running the dishwasher. Nice that it has filters you can clean but unless you actually read the manual you would never know you needed to do that, and given the poor print quality of the instructions, my guess is few will read them. Probably better off looking on line. Check back in 10 years and we'll see if it holds up.

Sentence (English): It replaced our 17+ years old KitchenAid dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Nice Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || It replaced our 17+ years old KitchenAid dishwasher. We had this dishwasher for over 11 months now and are happy with its performance. It takes a while figure out how to load various things but it's my experience that we can fit in more things and certain large or oddball shaped things that we could not fit into our previous dishwasher. As far as noise level of the dishwasher, its not silent but its quiet enough to have conversation at normal level while its running or if you run it in the middle of the night it is quiet enough to not disturb you if your bedroom happens to be near the kitchen area. Just be aware that if your dishwasher is not right next to the kitchen sink counter you may be charged extra for the installation. Our existing dishwasher was about 2 cabinet space away and we had to pay additional $150 for installation, even though all they had to do was replace the existing discharge hose. It would have been better if Costco installation policy would spell this out more clearly.

Sentence (English): Product Name: Media Electric Dishwasher.
Comments (English): Product Name: Media Electric Dishwasher. Model Name: MD-32SS. Capacity: 3 people. Release Year: 2021. Regular Voltage: 220V~, 60Hz. Power Consumption: 730W. Product Size: W435mm X D420mm H435mm. Product Weight: 14kg. Hello, let me introduce my family. I live with a husband who eats lunch and dinner every day, a 10-month-old who mixes formula and baby food, and a 4-year-old who eats breakfast and dinner. Our house is always overflowing with dishes. We're an average family that easily finishes 10kg of rice a month! I've always considered dishwashing my own responsibility and diligently done it, but after giving birth, my wrists are in bad shape. And because I keep putting off washing dishes because of childcare, I've been looking into a dishwasher. Then, I received a great opportunity to try out the Media no-installation dishwasher. Although I received it for free, I'll write a review based on my experience using it. I'd never used a dishwasher before because it was expensive, didn't clean cleanly, and had been rumored to have a peculiar smell. But now I've found a dishwasher that shatters all my stereotypes: the Media Dishwasher! Let me introduce its advantages! 1. Powerful cleaning power. The most important thing about a dishwasher is how well it cleans and how residue-free it is. But there's really no need to worry. It cleans so thoroughly. When I first started using the dishwasher, I used to just wipe off almost all the dirt with a blister pack before using it. Now, I just roughly wipe it down and run it through the dishwasher. Whether I use a blister pack or not, it's still clean before and after! I think it's because the Media Dishwasher's high-pressure rotary jet system sprays powerful water from the top and bottom pumps! I'm very satisfied. 2. No peculiar smell. In the past, dishes in my dishwasher had a smell, but with the Media Dishwasher, there's no smell! It washes with hot water at 72 degrees Celsius, so the only smell is the fragrant detergent. 3. Various washing modes. I love that I can choose the washing mode based on the food I ate that day and the condition of the dishes. There are five functions: 1. Standard wash, 2. Power wash, 3. Eco wash, 4. Quick wash, and 5. Steam sterilization. I usually use the standard wash, but I only use the steam sterilization for my children's bottles and dishes! Then, I can use dishes that are as clean as new. 4. Easy installation and a pretty design. Even women can easily assemble it! The fact that it's a no-punch machine makes it easy to install even if you don't live at home. I installed it by myself in less than 10 minutes when my husband wasn't home. And because I keep putting off washing dishes because of childcare, I've been looking into a dishwasher. Then, I received a great opportunity to try out the Media no-installation dishwasher. Although I received it for free, I'll write a review based on my experience using it. I'd never used a dishwasher before because it was expensive, didn't clean cleanly, and had been rumored to have a peculiar smell. But now I've found a dishwasher that shatters all my stereotypes: the Media Dishwasher! Let me introduce its advantages! 1. Powerful cleaning power. The most important thing about a dishwasher is how well it cleans and how residue-free it is. But there's really no need to worry. It cleans so thoroughly. When I first started using the dishwasher, I used to just wipe off almost all the dirt with a blister pack before using it. Now, I just roughly wipe it down and run it through the dishwasher. Whether I use a blister pack or not, it's still clean before and after! I think it's because the Media Dishwasher's high-pressure rotary jet system sprays powerful water from the top and bottom pumps! I'm very satisfied. 2. No peculiar smell. In the past, dishes in my dishwasher had a smell, but with the Media Dishwasher, there's no smell! It washes with hot water at 72 degrees Celsius, so the only smell is the fragrant detergent. 3. Various washing modes. I love that I can choose the washing mode based on the food I ate that day and the condition of the dishes. There are five functions: 1. Standard wash, 2. Power wash, 3. Eco wash, 4. Quick wash, and 5. Steam sterilization. I usually use the standard wash, but I only use the steam sterilization for my children's bottles and dishes! Then, I can use dishes that are as clean as new. 4. Easy installation and a pretty design. Even women can easily assemble it! The fact that it's a no-punch machine makes it easy to install even if you don't live at home. I installed it by myself in less than 10 minutes when my husband wasn't home. Now, there's only one drawback. Since it's a small dishwasher designed for three people, it won't fit large dishes. Since it's a three-person dishwasher, it's small, so large frying pans or dishes won't fit. So I wash the large dishes separately, and compared to before, the amount of dishes I wash has been cut in half, so it's not that inconvenient. For me! I'd recommend this to people who don't own a house, newlyweds, people who live alone, and mothers raising children. When you raise a child, especially a newborn, you use a lot of bottles, so you have to constantly wash them. I wash the bottles after the baby and repeat every day! Having a dishwasher can change your quality of life. And people who hate doing dishes and people who live alone can feel 100% satisfied if they use it! Although I received it for free, I'll write a review based on my experience using it. I'd never used a dishwasher before because it was expensive, didn't clean cleanly, and had been rumored to have a peculiar smell. But now I've found a dishwasher that shatters all my stereotypes: the Media Dishwasher! Let me introduce its advantages! 1. Powerful cleaning power. The most important thing about a dishwasher is how well it cleans and how residue-free it is. But there's really no need to worry. It cleans so thoroughly. When I first started using the dishwasher, I used to just wipe off almost all the dirt with a blister pack before using it. Now, I just roughly wipe it down and run it through the dishwasher. Whether I use a blister pack or not, it's still clean before and after! I think it's because the Media Dishwasher's high-pressure rotary jet system sprays powerful water from the top and bottom pumps! I'm very satisfied. 2. No peculiar smell. In the past, dishes in my dishwasher had a smell, but with the Media Dishwasher, there's no smell! It washes with hot water at 72 degrees Celsius, so the only smell is the fragrant detergent. 3. Various washing modes. I love that I can choose the washing mode based on the food I ate that day and the condition of the dishes. There are five functions: 1. Standard wash, 2. Power wash, 3. Eco wash, 4. Quick wash, and 5. Steam sterilization. I usually use the standard wash, but I only use the steam sterilization for my children's bottles and dishes! Then, I can use dishes that are as clean as new. 4. Easy installation and a pretty design. Even women can easily assemble it! The fact that it's a no-punch machine makes it easy to install even if you don't live at home. I installed it by myself in less than 10 minutes when my husband wasn't home. Now, there's only one drawback. Since it's a small dishwasher designed for three people, it won't fit large dishes. Since it's a three-person dishwasher, it's small, so large frying pans or dishes won't fit. So I wash the large dishes separately, and compared to before, the amount of dishes I wash has been cut in half, so it's not that inconvenient. For me! I'd recommend this to people who don't own a house, newlyweds, people who live alone, and mothers raising children. When you raise a child, especially a newborn, you use a lot of bottles, so you have to constantly wash them. I wash the bottles after the baby and repeat every day! Having a dishwasher can change your quality of life. And people who hate doing dishes and people who live alone can feel 100% satisfied if they use it! Product Size: W435mm X D420mm H435mm. Product Weight: 14kg. Hello, let me introduce my family. I live with a husband who eats lunch and dinner every day, a 10-month-old who mixes formula and baby food, and a 4-year-old who eats breakfast and dinner. Our house is always overflowing with dishes. We're an average family that easily finishes 10kg of rice a month! I've always considered dishwashing my own responsibility and diligently done it, but after giving birth, my wrists are in bad shape. And because I keep putting off washing dishes because of childcare, I've been looking into a dishwasher. Then, I received a great opportunity to try out the Media no-installation dishwasher. Although I received it for free, I'll write a review based on my experience using it. I'd never used a dishwasher before because it was expensive, didn't clean cleanly, and had been rumored to have a peculiar smell. But now I've found a dishwasher that shatters all my stereotypes: the Media Dishwasher! Let me introduce its advantages! 1. Powerful cleaning power. The most important thing about a dishwasher is how well it cleans and how residue-free it is. But there's really no need to worry. It cleans so thoroughly. When I first started using the dishwasher, I used to just wipe off almost all the dirt with a blister pack before using it. Now, I just roughly wipe it down and run it through the dishwasher. Whether I use a blister pack or not, it's still clean before and after! I think it's because the Media Dishwasher's high-pressure rotary jet system sprays powerful water from the top and bottom pumps! I'm very satisfied. 2. No peculiar smell. In the past, dishes in my dishwasher had a smell, but with the Media Dishwasher, there's no smell! It washes with hot water at 72 degrees Celsius, so the only smell is the fragrant detergent. 3. Various washing modes. I love that I can choose the washing mode based on the food I ate that day and the condition of the dishes. There are five functions: 1. Standard wash, 2. Power wash, 3. Eco wash, 4. Quick wash, and 5. Steam sterilization. I usually use the standard wash, but I only use the steam sterilization for my children's bottles and dishes! Then, I can use dishes that are as clean as new. 4. Easy installation and a pretty design. Even women can easily assemble it! The fact that it's a no-punch machine makes it easy to install even if you don't live at home. I installed it by myself in less than 10 minutes when my husband wasn't home. Now, there's only one drawback. Since it's a small dishwasher designed for three people, it won't fit large dishes. Since it's a three-person dishwasher, it's small, so large frying pans or dishes won't fit. So I wash the large dishes separately, and compared to before, the amount of dishes I wash has been cut in half, so it's not that inconvenient. For me! I'd recommend this to people who don't own a house, newlyweds, people who live alone, and mothers raising children. When you raise a child, especially a newborn, you use a lot of bottles, so you have to constantly wash them. I wash the bottles after the baby and repeat every day! Having a dishwasher can change your quality of life. And people who hate doing dishes and people who live alone can feel 100% satisfied if they use it! This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

I live with a husband who eats lunch and dinner every day, a 10-month-old who mixes formula and baby food, and a 4-year-old who eats breakfast and dinner. Our house is always overflowing with dishes. We're an average family that easily finishes 10kg of rice a month! I've always considered dishwashing my own responsibility and diligently done it, but after giving birth, my wrists are in bad shape. And because I keep putting off washing dishes because of childcare, I've been looking into a dishwasher. Then, I received a great opportunity to try out the Media no-installation dishwasher. Although I received it for free, I'll write a review based on my experience using it. I'd never used a dishwasher before because it was expensive, didn't clean cleanly, and had been rumored to have a peculiar smell. But now I've found a dishwasher that shatters all my stereotypes: the Media Dishwasher! Let me introduce its advantages! 1. Powerful cleaning power. The most important thing about a dishwasher is how well it cleans and how residue-free it is. But there's really no need to worry. It cleans so thoroughly. When I first started using the dishwasher, I used to just wipe off almost all the dirt with a blister pack before using it. Now, I just roughly wipe it down and run it through the dishwasher. Whether I use a blister pack or not, it's still clean before and after! I think it's because the Media Dishwasher's high-pressure rotary jet system sprays powerful water from the top and bottom pumps! I'm very satisfied. 2. No peculiar smell. In the past, dishes in my dishwasher had a smell, but with the Media Dishwasher, there's no smell! It washes with hot water at 72 degrees Celsius, so the only smell is the fragrant detergent. 3. Various washing modes. I love that I can choose the washing mode based on the food I ate that day and the condition of the dishes. There are five functions: 1. Standard wash, 2. Power wash, 3. Eco wash, 4. Quick wash, and 5. Steam sterilization. I usually use the standard wash, but I only use the steam sterilization for my children's bottles and dishes! Then, I can use dishes that are as clean as new. 4. Easy installation and a pretty design. Even women can easily assemble it! The fact that it's a no-punch machine makes it easy to install even if you don't live at home. I installed it by myself in less than 10 minutes when my husband wasn't home. Now, there's only one drawback. Since it's a small dishwasher designed for three people, it won't fit large dishes. Since it's a three-person dishwasher, it's small, so large frying pans or dishes won't fit. So I wash the large dishes separately, and compared to before, the amount of dishes I wash has been cut in half, so it's not that inconvenient. For me! I'd recommend this to people who don't own a house, newlyweds, people who live alone, and mothers raising children. When you raise a child, especially a newborn, you use a lot of bottles, so you have to constantly wash them. I wash the bottles after the baby and repeat every day! Having a dishwasher can change your quality of life. And people who hate doing dishes and people who live alone can feel 100% satisfied if they use it! I live with a husband who eats lunch and dinner every day, a 10-month-old who mixes formula and baby food, and a 4-year-old who eats breakfast and dinner. Our house is always overflowing with dishes. We're an average family that easily finishes 10kg of rice a month! I've always considered dishwashing my own responsibility and diligently done it, but after giving birth, my wrists are in bad shape. And because I keep putting off washing dishes because of childcare, I've been looking into a dishwasher. Then, I received a great opportunity to try out the Media no-installation dishwasher. Although I received it for free, I'll write a review based on my experience using it. I'd never used a dishwasher before because it was expensive, didn't clean cleanly, and had been rumored to have a peculiar smell. But now I've found a dishwasher that shatters all my stereotypes: the Media Dishwasher! Let me introduce its advantages! 1. Powerful cleaning power. The most important thing about a dishwasher is how well it cleans and how residue-free it is. But there's really no need to worry. It cleans so thoroughly. When I first started using the dishwasher, I used to just wipe off almost all the dirt with a blister pack before using it. Now, I just roughly wipe it down and run it through the dishwasher. Whether I use a blister pack or not, it's still clean before and after! I think it's because the Media Dishwasher's high-pressure rotary jet system sprays powerful water from the top and bottom pumps! I'm very satisfied. 2. No peculiar smell. In the past, dishes in my dishwasher had a smell, but with the Media Dishwasher, there's no smell! It washes with hot water at 72 degrees Celsius, so the only smell is the fragrant detergent. 3. Various washing modes. I love that I can choose the washing mode based on the food I ate that day and the condition of the dishes. There are five functions: 1. Standard wash, 2. Power wash, 3. Eco wash, 4. Quick wash, and 5. Steam sterilization. I usually use the standard wash, but I only use the steam sterilization for my children's bottles and dishes! Then, I can use dishes that are as clean as new. 4. Easy installation and a pretty design. Even women can easily assemble it! The fact that it's a no-punch machine makes it easy to install even if you don't live at home. I installed it by myself in less than 10 minutes when my husband wasn't home. Now, there's only one drawback. Since it's a small dishwasher designed for three people, it won't fit large dishes. Since it's a three-person dishwasher, it's small, so large frying pans or dishes won't fit. So I wash the large dishes separately, and compared to before, the amount of dishes I wash has been cut in half, so it's not that inconvenient. For me! I'd recommend this to people who don't own a house, newlyweds, people who live alone, and mothers raising children. When you raise a child, especially a newborn, you use a lot of bottles, so you have to constantly wash them. I wash the bottles after the baby and repeat every day! Having a dishwasher can change your quality of life. And people who hate doing dishes and people who live alone can feel 100% satisfied if they use it! This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

I live with a husband who eats lunch and dinner every day, a 10-month-old who mixes formula and baby food, and a 4-year-old who eats breakfast and dinner. Our house is always overflowing with dishes. We're an average family that easily finishes 10kg of rice a month! I've always considered dishwashing my own responsibility and diligently done it, but after giving birth, my wrists are in bad shape. And because I keep putting off washing dishes because of childcare, I've been looking into a dishwasher. Then, I received a great opportunity to try out the Media no-installation dishwasher. Although I received it for free, I'll write a review based on my experience using it. I'd never used a dishwasher before because it was expensive, didn't clean cleanly, and had been rumored to have a peculiar smell. But now I've found a dishwasher that shatters all my stereotypes: the Media Dishwasher! Let me introduce its advantages! 1. Powerful cleaning power. The most important thing about a dishwasher is how well it cleans and how residue-free it is. But there's really no need to worry. It cleans so thoroughly. When I first started using the dishwasher, I used to just wipe off almost all the dirt with a blister pack before using it. Now, I just roughly wipe it down and run it through the dishwasher. Whether I use a blister pack or not, it's still clean before and after! I think it's because the Media Dishwasher's high-pressure rotary jet system sprays powerful water from the top and bottom pumps! I'm very satisfied. 2. No peculiar smell. In the past, dishes in my dishwasher had a smell, but with the Media Dishwasher, there's no smell! It washes with hot water at 72 degrees Celsius, so the only smell is the fragrant detergent. 3. Various washing modes. I love that I can choose the washing mode based on the food I ate that day and the condition of the dishes. There are five functions: 1. Standard wash, 2. Power wash, 3. Eco wash, 4. Quick wash, and 5. Steam sterilization. I usually use the standard wash, but I only use the steam sterilization for my children's bottles and dishes! Then, I can use dishes that are as clean as new. 4. Easy installation and a pretty design. Even women can easily assemble it! The fact that it's a no-punch machine makes it easy to install even if you don't live at home. I installed it by myself in less than 10 minutes when my husband wasn't home. Now, there's only one drawback. Since it's a small dishwasher designed for three people, it won't fit large dishes. Since it's a three-person dishwasher, it's small, so large frying pans or dishes won't fit. So I wash the large dishes separately, and compared to before, the amount of dishes I wash has been cut in half, so it's not that inconvenient. For me! I'd recommend this to people who don't own a house, newlyweds, people who live alone, and mothers raising children. When you raise a child, especially a newborn, you use a lot of bottles, so you have to constantly wash them. I wash the bottles after the baby and repeat every day! Having a dishwasher can change your quality of life. And people who hate doing dishes and people who live alone can feel 100% satisfied if they use it! Although I received it for free, I'll write a review based on my experience using it. I'd never used a dishwasher before because it was expensive, didn't clean cleanly, and had been rumored to have a peculiar smell. But now I've found a dishwasher that shatters all my stereotypes: the Media Dishwasher! Let me introduce its advantages! 1. Powerful cleaning power. The most important thing about a dishwasher is how well it cleans and how residue-free it is. But there's really no need to worry. It cleans so thoroughly. Whether I use a blister pack or not, it's still clean before and after! I think it's because the Media Dishwasher's high-pressure rotary jet system sprays powerful water from the top and bottom pumps! I'm very satisfied. 2. No peculiar smell. In the past, dishes in my dishwasher had a smell, but with the Media Dishwasher, there's no smell! It washes with hot water at 72 degrees Celsius, so the only smell is the fragrant detergent. 3. Various washing modes. I love that I can choose the washing mode based on the food I ate that day and the condition of the dishes. There are five functions: 1. Standard wash, 2. Power wash, 3. Eco wash, 4. Quick wash, and 5. Steam sterilization. I usually use the standard wash, but I only use the steam sterilization for my children's bottles and dishes! Then, I can use dishes that are as clean as new. 4. Easy installation and a pretty design. Even women can easily assemble it! The fact that it's a no-punch machine makes it easy to install even if you don't live at home. I installed it by myself in less than 10 minutes when my husband wasn't home. Now, there's only one drawback. Since it's a small dishwasher designed for three people, it won't fit large dishes. Since it's a three-person dishwasher, it's small, so large frying pans or dishes won't fit. So I wash the large dishes separately, and compared to before, the amount of dishes I wash has been cut in half, so it's not that inconvenient. For me! I'd recommend this to people who don't own a house, newlyweds, people who live alone, and mothers raising children. When you raise a child, especially a newborn, you use a lot of bottles, so you have to constantly wash them. I wash the bottles after the baby and repeat every day! Having a dishwasher can change your quality of life. And people who hate doing dishes and people who live alone can feel 100% satisfied if they use it! And because I keep putting off washing dishes because of childcare, I've been looking into a dishwasher. Then, I received a great opportunity to try out the Media no-installation dishwasher. Although I received it for free, I'll write a review based on my experience using it. I'd never used a dishwasher before because it was expensive, didn't clean cleanly, and had been rumored to have a peculiar smell. But now I've found a dishwasher that shatters all my stereotypes: the Media Dishwasher! Let me introduce its advantages! 1. Powerful cleaning power. The most important thing about a dishwasher is how well it cleans and how residue-free it is. But there's really no need to worry. It cleans so thoroughly. When I first started using the dishwasher, I used to just wipe off almost all the dirt with a blister pack before using it. Now, I just roughly wipe it down and run it through the dishwasher. Whether I use a blister pack or not, it's still clean before and after! I think it's because the Media Dishwasher's high-pressure rotary jet system sprays powerful water from the top and bottom pumps! I'm very satisfied. 2. No peculiar smell. In the past, dishes in my dishwasher had a smell, but with the Media Dishwasher, there's no smell! It washes with hot water at 72 degrees Celsius, so the only smell is the fragrant detergent. 3. Various washing modes. I love that I can choose the washing mode based on the food I ate that day and the condition of the dishes. There are five functions: 1. Standard wash, 2. Power wash, 3. Eco wash, 4. Quick wash, and 5. Steam sterilization. I usually use the standard wash, but I only use the steam sterilization for my children's bottles and dishes! Then, I can use dishes that are as clean as new. 4. Easy installation and a pretty design. Even women can easily assemble it! The fact that it's a no-punch machine makes it easy to install even if you don't live at home. I installed it by myself in less than 10 minutes when my husband wasn't home. Now, there's only one drawback. Since it's a small dishwasher designed for three people, it won't fit large dishes. Since it's a three-person dishwasher, it's small, so large frying pans or dishes won't fit. So I wash the large dishes separately, and compared to before, the amount of dishes I wash has been cut in half, so it's not that inconvenient. For me! I'd recommend this to people who don't own a house, newlyweds, people who live alone, and mothers raising children. When you raise a child, especially a newborn, you use a lot of bottles, so you have to constantly wash them. I wash the bottles after the baby and repeat every day! Having a dishwasher can change your quality of life. And people who hate doing dishes and people who live alone can feel 100% satisfied if they use it! I think it's because the Media Dishwasher's high-pressure rotary jet system sprays powerful water from the top and bottom pumps! I'm very satisfied. 2. No peculiar smell. Comments (English): Product Name: Media Electric Dishwasher. Model Name: MD-32SS. Capacity: 3 people. Release Year: 2021. Regular Voltage: 220V~, 60Hz. Power Consumption: 730W. Product Size: W435mm X D420mm H435mm. Product Weight: 14kg. Hello, let me introduce my family. I live with a husband who eats lunch and dinner every day, a 10-month-old who mixes formula and baby food, and a 4-year-old who eats breakfast and dinner. Our house is always overflowing with dishes. We're an average family that easily finishes 10kg of rice a month! I've always considered dishwashing my own responsibility and diligently done it, but after giving birth, my wrists are in bad shape. And because I keep putting off washing dishes because of childcare, I've been looking into a dishwasher. Then, I received a great opportunity to try out the Media no-installation dishwasher. Although I received it for free, I'll write a review based on my experience using it. I'd never used a dishwasher before because it was expensive, didn't clean cleanly, and had been rumored to have a peculiar smell. But now I've found a dishwasher that shatters all my stereotypes: the Media Dishwasher! Let me introduce its advantages! 1. Powerful cleaning power. The most important thing about a dishwasher is how well it cleans and how residue-free it is. But there's really no need to worry. It cleans so thoroughly. When I first started using the dishwasher, I used to just wipe off almost all the dirt with a blister pack before using it. Now, I just roughly wipe it down and run it through the dishwasher. Whether I use a blister pack or not, it's still clean before and after! I think it's because the Media Dishwasher's high-pressure rotary jet system sprays powerful water from the top and bottom pumps! I'm very satisfied. 2. No peculiar smell. In the past, dishes in my dishwasher had a smell, but with the Media Dishwasher, there's no smell! It washes with hot water at 72 degrees Celsius, so the only smell is the fragrant detergent. 3. Various washing modes. I love that I can choose the washing mode based on the food I ate that day and the condition of the dishes. There are five functions: 1. Standard wash, 2. Power wash, 3. Eco wash, 4. Quick wash, and 5. Steam sterilization. I usually use the standard wash, but I only use the steam sterilization for my children's bottles and dishes! Then, I can use dishes that are as clean as new. 4. Easy installation and a pretty design. Even women can easily assemble it! The fact that it's a no-punch machine makes it easy to install even if you don't live at home. I installed it by myself in less than 10 minutes when my husband wasn't home. Now, there's only one drawback. Since it's a small dishwasher designed for three people, it won't fit large dishes. Since it's a three-person dishwasher, it's small, so large frying pans or dishes won't fit. So I wash the large dishes separately, and compared to before, the amount of dishes I wash has been cut in half, so it's not that inconvenient. For me! I'd recommend this to people who don't own a house, newlyweds, people who live alone, and mothers raising children. When you raise a child, especially a newborn, you use a lot of bottles, so you have to constantly wash them. I wash the bottles after the baby and repeat every day! Having a dishwasher can change your quality of life. And people who hate doing dishes and people who live alone can feel 100% satisfied if they use it! Comments (English): Product Name: Media Electric Dishwasher. Model Name: MD-32SS. Capacity: 3 people. Release Year: 2021. Regular Voltage: 220V~, 60Hz. Power Consumption: 730W. I live with a husband who eats lunch and dinner every day, a 10-month-old who mixes formula and baby food, and a 4-year-old who eats breakfast and dinner. Our house is always overflowing with dishes. We're an average family that easily finishes 10kg of rice a month! I've always considered dishwashing my own responsibility and diligently done it, but after giving birth, my wrists are in bad shape. And because I keep putting off washing dishes because of childcare, I've been looking into a dishwasher. Then, I received a great opportunity to try out the Media no-installation dishwasher. Although I received it for free, I'll write a review based on my experience using it. I'd never used a dishwasher before because it was expensive, didn't clean cleanly, and had been rumored to have a peculiar smell. But now I've found a dishwasher that shatters all my stereotypes: the Media Dishwasher! Let me introduce its advantages! 1. Powerful cleaning power. The most important thing about a dishwasher is how well it cleans and how residue-free it is. But there's really no need to worry. It cleans so thoroughly. When I first started using the dishwasher, I used to just wipe off almost all the dirt with a blister pack before using it. Now, I just roughly wipe it down and run it through the dishwasher. Whether I use a blister pack or not, it's still clean before and after! I think it's because the Media Dishwasher's high-pressure rotary jet system sprays powerful water from the top and bottom pumps! I'm very satisfied. 2. No peculiar smell. In the past, dishes in my dishwasher had a smell, but with the Media Dishwasher, there's no smell! It washes with hot water at 72 degrees Celsius, so the only smell is the fragrant detergent. 3. Various washing modes. I love that I can choose the washing mode based on the food I ate that day and the condition of the dishes. There are five functions: 1. Standard wash, 2. Power wash, 3. Eco wash, 4. Quick wash, and 5. Steam sterilization. I usually use the standard wash, but I only use the steam sterilization for my children's bottles and dishes! Then, I can use dishes that are as clean as new. 4. Easy installation and a pretty design. Even women can easily assemble it! The fact that it's a no-punch machine makes it easy to install even if you don't live at home. I installed it by myself in less than 10 minutes when my husband wasn't home. Now, there's only one drawback. Since it's a small dishwasher designed for three people, it won't fit large dishes. Since it's a three-person dishwasher, it's small, so large frying pans or dishes won't fit. So I wash the large dishes separately, and compared to before, the amount of dishes I wash has been cut in half, so it's not that inconvenient. For me! I'd recommend this to people who don't own a house, newlyweds, people who live alone, and mothers raising children. When you raise a child, especially a newborn, you use a lot of bottles, so you have to constantly wash them. I wash the bottles after the baby and repeat every day! Having a dishwasher can change your quality of life. And people who hate doing dishes and people who live alone can feel 100% satisfied if they use it! This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

Whether I use a blister pack or not, it's still clean before and after! I think it's because the Media Dishwasher's high-pressure rotary jet system sprays powerful water from the top and bottom pumps! I'm very satisfied. 2. No peculiar smell. In the past, dishes in my dishwasher had a smell, but with the Media Dishwasher, there's no smell! It washes with hot water at 72 degrees Celsius, so the only smell is the fragrant detergent. 3. Various washing modes. I love that I can choose the washing mode based on the food I ate that day and the condition of the dishes. There are five functions: 1. Standard wash, 2. Power wash, 3. Eco wash, 4. Quick wash, and 5. Steam sterilization. I usually use the standard wash, but I only use the steam sterilization for my children's bottles and dishes! Then, I can use dishes that are as clean as new. 4. Easy installation and a pretty design. Even women can easily assemble it! Now, there's only one drawback. Since it's a small dishwasher designed for three people, it won't fit large dishes. So I wash the large dishes separately, and compared to before, the amount of dishes I wash has been cut in half, so it's not that inconvenient. For me! I'd recommend this to people who don't own a house, newlyweds, people who live alone, and mothers raising children. When you raise a child, especially a newborn, you use a lot of bottles, so you have to constantly wash them. I wash the bottles after the baby and repeat every day!
